title: A periodic counterexample to the diffuse allocation characterization
description:
An explicit periodic diffuse measure on R^2 has a rooted law invariant under every measurable, pointwise-covariant, measure-preserving allocation determined by its original observed state, but fails the full joint mass-stationarity identity. The measure consists of horizontal Lebesgue lines with alternating densities one and two. Covariance and a finite per-period mass equation cover all allocations, including noninjective maps. In the defining unit-square mass-resampling experiment, the heavy-root event has probability two thirds instead of zero. A constant accompanying random element suffices. This gives a negative answer to Thorisson's historical Problem 4.1 and Last-Thorisson's Problem 7.5 in their stated unrestricted scope.

The entire existential negative conclusion is an elementary consequence of Last-Thorisson (2009), Example 7.1, their Lebesgue-product mass-stationarity proposition already in arXiv:1405.7566v1 (2014), Section 8 Proposition 1, retained in the 2015 version, and the full allocation-transfer calculation displayed in the note. Last-Thorisson (2023), Section 8 and Remark 8.1, give the canonical diffuse parallel-line/invariant-direction balancing obstruction; Khezeli-Mellick (2025), final Remark 3.2, explicitly identifies the product/atomic-quotient balancing-allocation reduction. Those balancing-existence statements have a distinct scope from the self-preserving characterization. The periodic rational-weight model is an elementary worked illustration of these established mechanisms. No new-discovery, novelty, firstness, exhaustive-priority or worldwide-current-openness claim is made. The first explicit recognition of the combined corollary and priority of the exact periodic formula remain unestablished by bounded searches.

The example is singular, two-dimensional and has a continuous translation stabilizer. It supplies no counterexample for positive-density measures, one-dimensional diffuse measures, free actions, absence of invariant directions, independent stationary backgrounds, or invariance under all preserving Markov kernels. An explicit preserving Markov kernel changes its rooted type. The exact pointwise-covariance convention is essential; an unspecified spatial-almost-everywhere representative with an unrestricted root value is a different formulation.

The deposit contains a four-page research note and a verification archive with editable source, all twenty-six frozen original files and both original evidence ZIPs, independent mathematical and bounded priority audits, source-version fingerprints, a closed-inventory verifier and a deterministic builder. Default normal and optimized finite replay is distinguished from optional provenance authentication of three complete original corpora and five original primary PDFs; additional primary-edition fingerprints and inspection records are supplied separately. Third-party publications, extracted source text, raw corpus records, page images and private credentials are excluded. Finite computations and hashes supplement the analytic proof and do not certify novelty. Compressed-byte reproducibility requires identical inputs and the same Python ZIP implementation and zlib runtime.

AI tools were used extensively in mathematical development, source review, writing, computation and adversarial checking. The recorded adversarial reviews were performed by AI agents. This is an unrefereed preprint; no completed independent human peer review or formal proof-assistant verification is claimed. The author is responsible for the claims.

title: Near-one oriented-percolation flow from Bernoulli first-passage estimates
description:
For the canonical square-lattice oriented Bernoulli edge-capacity flow, the note derives 1-v(p)~sqrt(2(1-p)) as p increases to one, the asymptotic posed by Aldous and Lenderman in 2004. The sources are the left and bottom boundaries excluding the top-left and bottom-right sink corners; the sinks are the top and right boundaries. Shared vertices are allowed among edge-disjoint paths. The exact finite directed-cut identity, its bounded boundary terms, and the fixed-parameter volume limit followed by the small-defect limit are supplied. The source-stated deterministic L1 flow-density limit is an explicit input; the expectation limit also follows from diagonal superadditivity.

The entire asymptotic is presented as an explicitly attributed corollary of Basdevant-Gouere-Theret's public 2021 strict-site score scaling and weighted-list computation in arXiv:2106.12266v1, Section 3.3, equation (33), with its m=0 numerical terms. A precise model-event inclusion groups outgoing rare-edge marks into independent site marks of probability 2q-q^2. The ordinary undirected first-passage theorem alone is not substituted for the asymmetric cut model with zero-cost backward traversals. This is an application identifying an older-estimate consequence, not a new central rare-defect, Poisson, BK or detour estimate. No novelty, historical-firstness, exhaustive-priority or present-day-openness claim is made. An earlier explicit statement of this particular flow corollary was not located in bounded searches; its first recognition remains unestablished. Exact equation references were checked in the public 2021 v1, not in a retrieved final journal body.

The deposit contains the research note and a verification archive with editable source, all thirty immutable original files and their proof/audit history, the longer BK-Poisson argument, independent mathematical and bounded priority assessments, finite falsification controls, source fingerprints, closed typed inventories, an isolated archival replay launcher and a deterministic ZIP builder. The current launcher distinguishes historical requested flags from measured isolated execution flags. Optional source-only authentication checks all three complete native corpora and four exact primary bodies without executing archival code; those third-party bodies and raw corpora are excluded from the deposit. Finite checks and cryptographic hashes supplement the analytic proof and do not prove the asymptotic or novelty. Compressed-byte reproducibility requires identical inputs and the same Python ZIP implementation and zlib runtime.

The claim concerns the prescribed edge-capacity model, not vertex-disjoint flow, other boundary conventions or other graph families. Classical Poisson-chain and product-BK inputs, and Verges's 2025 overlapping-region decomposition/skeleton work, are credited for the preserved alternative proof. title: An explicit rank-two entropy-minimizing Fano degeneration
description:
We give an explicit smooth Fano fivefold whose unique global Han–Li entropy-minimizing valuation has rational rank two and is therefore nondivisorial. Its canonical first central variety is singular, so this first degeneration is nontrivial. The example is the product of Miao–Wang's established quadric-blowup threefold with the first Hirzebruch surface. Exact moment equations specify the two positive weights. A universal resultant argument and the classical Hermite–Lindemann theorem prove that their ratio is irrational. The associated graded anticanonical ring, canonical weight normalization, weak product soliton equation, and application of the established global optimality criterion are made explicit.

The construction satisfies the request discussed by Blum in Oberwolfach Report 17/2022, pp. 888–889, without a dimension bound or a product exclusion. Major inputs are due to Miao–Wang, Wang–Zhu, Han–Li, and Blum–Liu–Xu–Zhuang. Earlier nontrivial first centers of Li–Li are credited; their second example's rational rank was not certified in the sources inspected. The threefold factor was already announced in Miao–Wang's January 2024 preprint. No novelty, historical firstness, exhaustive priority, or continued-openness certificate is claimed.

AI tools were used extensively in developing, checking, and preparing the work. The reported adversarial reviews were performed by AI agents. This is an unrefereed preprint; independent human peer review and formal verification have not been completed. The accompanying verification archive preserves original proof and correction bytes, source fingerprints, bounded priority audits, adversarial analyses, and exact auxiliary diagnostics. Passing software checks does not formally verify the geometric or analytic theorem inputs.

title: Post-Lie nonexistence with a semisimple target
description: A proof of a unimodular-source obstruction for transverse pairs of homomorphisms into a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra. The perfect nonsemisimple-source post-Lie nonexistence statement follows as a corollary. The argument uses a holomorphic determinant relative invariant and classical Lie-group topology, with explicit attribution of Baues's affine-space predecessor and the earlier post-Lie literature. AI systems were used extensively in solving, checking and writing the work. This is an unrefereed preprint; no completed human peer review, formal verification, historical firstness or exhaustive literature coverage is claimed.

title: NP-completeness of three-terminal shortest-path blocking
description:
We prove NP-completeness of undirected, unit-traversal-length three-terminal Blocking Shortest Paths: delete a minimum edge set to increase every pairwise terminal distance by at least one. Hardness holds with unit deletion costs and all three original terminal distances equal to three. A direct Vertex Cover reduction also proves NP-completeness when all terminal distances must remain finite, or increase exactly from three to four. The result classifies the undirected triangle question posed by Stefan Krause in 2005. The classical subdivision identity is credited to Poljak (1974), and the related tripartite attachment mechanism to Khachiyan and coauthors (2008). Historical first priority and continued open status through 2026 are not asserted.

This unrefereed research note includes a source and verification archive with the unchanged original proof packet, explicit hash manifests, source-free standard-library Python reproduction, independent adversarial mathematical and computational audits, source-model checks and a bounded priority audit. title: A Robinson counterexample to ideal-only tangency certificates
description:
The classical Robinson sextic is globally nonnegative, but adding any nonnegative constant does not make it a finite sum of real polynomial squares modulo even the full ideal of polynomials vanishing on its real tangency variety. This refutes both the exact ordinary-radical certificate and the every-positive-epsilon original-ideal certificate proposed in the unrestricted tangency-minor formulation of Schweighofer's 2007 question. The same zero-line and coordinate-axis obstruction refutes the separate-cross-product reading printed in the report. Arbitrarily many summands of arbitrary degree are allowed. The attained example is within the unrestricted question; a separate nonattaining diagnostic concerns only the literal-product reading and uses a constant shift of the standard example in Schweighofer (2006), Section 1.6, equation (6). The standard sphere-minimization mechanism retains its attribution to Laurent's updated manuscript dated 6 February 2010, Section 7.2.3, Lemma 7.21, manuscript pages 117-118 (https://homepages.cwi.nl/~monique/files/moment-ima-update-new.pdf). The earlier 2009 published chapter has a different Lemma 7.21; its DOI is bibliographic context, not the tangency locator. Robinson's form and classical zero-set ingredients retain their attribution. The identical ten-zero cubic obstruction is explicitly credited to Reznick (2000), Section 4(b), printed page 259, authenticated in the author-hosted publisher reprint. Complete 2008 and 2009 Ha-Pham article texts were not obtained; truncated-certificate comparisons rely on later primary statements and the access gaps remain disclosed. The 66-record citation graph is a metadata screen with marked primary-text follow-ups. No author-approved formula correction, first bibliographic priority or continued open status through 2026 is asserted.
